record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of infinite dimensional algebras
record.original_question: Is every irreducible compact three-dimensional hyperbolic manifold virtually Haken, meaning that it has a finite-sheeted cover that is Haken; equivalently, does every cocompact lattice Gamma in SL(2,C) have a finite-index subgroup that is either a free product with amalgamation or an HNN construction?

evidence.quote: The Virtual Haken Conjecture. Every irreducible compact 3-dimensional hyperbolic manifold has a finite sheeted cover which is Haken, or, equivalently, every cocompact lattice Gamma in SL(2, C) has a finite index subgroup which is either a free product with amalgam, or an HNN-construction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A compact 3-manifold $M$ is called Haken if it is irreducible (every embedded 2-sphere bounds a 3-ball) and contains a properly embedded two-sided incompressible surface. $M$ is said to be virtually Haken if it admits a finite-sheeted covering space that is Haken.

Prove or disprove: every closed irreducible 3-dimensional hyperbolic manifold is virtually Haken. Equivalently, show that every cocompact lattice $\Gamma \le \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ has a finite-index subgroup that splits nontrivially as either an amalgamated free product $A *_C B$ or an HNN extension $A *_C$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Virtual Haken Conjecture was proved by Ian Agol in 2012 (building on work of Daniel Wise, Bergeron–Wise, Kahn–Markovic, Haglund–Wise, and others). Agol's paper "The virtual Haken conjecture" appeared in Documenta Mathematica 18 (2013), establishing the conjecture in full.

status_evidence.title: The virtual Haken conjecture - Agol
status_evidence.snippet: Agol, Ian. The virtual Haken conjecture. With an appendix by Ian Agol, Daniel Groves, and Jason Manning. Documenta Math. 18 (2013), 1045-1087.
status_evidence.claim: Agol proved the Virtual Haken Conjecture in 2012/2013.

status_evidence.title: Virtually Haken conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In March 2012, Ian Agol announced... that he had proved the virtually Haken conjecture for the case where M is closed (i.e., compact and without boundary).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is now a theorem.
